title: Low-energy room-temperature carbon dots for targeted sensing of MET inhibitor capmatinib
content:
RSC Adv., 2025, 15,28375-28383
DOI: 10.1039/D5RA04346H, Paper
Open Access
  This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 Unported Licence.
Mohamed N. Goda, Laila S. Alqarni, Hossieny Ibrahim, Al-Montaser Bellah H. Ali, Mohamed M. El-Wekil
Sensitive, cost-effective fluorescence method using NCDs (38.72% QY) enables selective fluorescence quenching-based detection of capmatinib (LOD 3.6 nM), showing high accuracy (97.4–105.3% recovery) and precision (RSD < 4.11%) in biological fluids.
